title.narrative: Increasing food production and agricultural outputs among vulnerable population

description.narrative: ltpgtThe humanitarian needs in Sudan are escalating as the dry season exacerbates vulnerabilities and the potential for further conflict intensifies. Since the outbreak of conflict between SAF and RSF on April 15, 2023, over 24,850 fatalities have been reported, according to ACLED (November 2024). The influx of IDPs into SPLM-N-controlled areas of Region 1 has placed immense pressure on limited resources. By September 2024,nbspSRRA estimated 788,137 registered refugees in the region. Representing a 32% population increase, with IDPs now comprising 24% of the population(FSMU, MSNA 2024 assessment)lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThis crisis is further compounded by the devastation from heavy rains, floods, and ongoing conflict, which have hindered food production and agricultural activities. Despite the seasonal end of the lean period in September, food security has shown marginal improvement. Historic flooding has destroyed crops, while conflict prevents planting, cultivation, and harvesting. Sudan is facing an unprecedented hunger crisis, with nearly 26 million people experiencing acute food insecurity and 755,000 at risk of famine-like conditions (IPC 5). Alarmingly, UNOCHA indicates extreme food insecurity among IDPs in besieged areas like Dilling and Western Kadugli in South Kordofan.ltbrgtIn response, DCA and its implementing partner aim to bolster food production and agricultural livelihoods in four counties: Western Kadugli, Thobo, Um Durrein, and Rief Ashergi. These interventions align with SHF priorities by addressing immediate food insecurity while strengthening resilience in conflict-affected areas.lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtKey Interventions:ltbrgtlt/pgtltulgtltligtltbgtAgricultural Inputs:lt/bgt Distribution of seeds and tools to 10,000 households (2,500 per county) to enhance immediate food production capacity.lt/ligtltligtltbgtFarmer Training:lt/bgt Training 400 lead farmers as ToT-snbsp(100 per county) to build local expertise and improve agricultural practices.lt/ligtltligtltbgtTree Nurseries:lt/bgt Establishment and support for eight tree nursery groups (two per county) to promote sustainable livelihoods and environmental recovery.lt/ligtltligtltbgtBeekeeping:lt/bgt Provision of bee hives and protective equipment to 80 individualsnbspto diversify income sources and foster resilience.lt/ligtlt/ulgtltpgtltbrgtBy combining immediate assistance with sustainable livelihoods, this project addresses the acute food needs of vulnerable populations while building local capacity to withstand future shocks. Furthermore, peacebuilding workshops will be mainstreamed into food security programming to foster social cohesion and mitigate tensions among displaced and host communities. The proposed activities directly target communities most affected by conflict and displacement, ensuring an inclusive, context-sensitive, and resilience-oriented response.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtThe activities are conducted in coordination with the local authorities(Secretariat of Agriculture) and other actors who work in agriculture(SP).lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtConflict sensitivity:ltbrgtDue to increasing tensions between IDP and host communities stemming from a due to lack of available resources DCA proposes to include activities on conflict sensitivity. Partners will be conducting trainings and awareness sessions among communities and leaders on social cohesion and importance of peaceful co-existence. The teams will focus on the community leaders and selection committee members who are trained in humanitarian principles, conflict resolution, importance on vulnerable population and assistance. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtDue to the increased influx of IDPs following, risks have emerged:ltbrgt- Increased pressure on natural resources and conflict between communities, especially for land and water resourcesltbrgt- Few resources of aid to IDPs and vulnerable host communities, creating conflict.ltbrgt- Local authorities undermining civil society and reduced space in implementation.ltbrgt- Lack of understanding of humanitarian principles by local authorities.ltbrgtDCA conflict sensitivity focal point is Head of Programmes (Nathan Akureje) who has received extensive training in CS in 2023 and 2024. Please find Annex A_Risk Matrix_2024nbspfor further informationltbrgtlt/pgt
